claims.text: POL-NS-01 is drafted as a conjunctive four-limb test and the driver side fails limb (c) on its own numbers. The dwell that counts is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the driver's 'arrived' tap. The pickup is STANDARD class (trip_record.pickup_zone_class), so the required continuous in-geofence dwell is 300 seconds; the driver's own trace shows exactly one qualifying in-radius run, from 19:33:50 to 19:37:40 — 230 seconds. Limb (c) therefore fails, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable under this clause. Note that this conclusion does not depend on where the rider was: even taking the driver's arrival marker entirely at face value, the hold is 70 seconds short.

POL-NS-06 states the arithmetic directly: minimum 300 seconds for the STANDARD class, measured 230 seconds, shortfall 70 seconds. Where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum, the fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, and no driver compensation is payable. The amount to refund is the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 recorded in the ledger, which is the whole contested sum.

The driver's only explanation for the short hold — 'I was stuck behind an accident' — has no evidential support and cannot rescue the dwell. I disclose the impairment: EV-ADVIS-00613-01 is MISSING, its status is MISSING and its weight_multiplier is 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact. POL-NS-06 permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory covering the pickup road is present and populated with an admissible type, and it expressly says a MISSING advisory makes that limb unavailable. Independently of the advisory, the trace shows run_count 1 and a single interval, so there is no second interval to accumulate in any event. The 70-second shortfall stands.

The rider is separately exonerated under POL-NS-04. At 19:08:40 she sent the trip's only chat message: 'where are you? I'm at Blk 12 pickup point' — a locating message naming her own position and block. The driver posted no reply within 120 seconds of it and placed no in-app call at any point before terminating; all three in-app calls in trip_record were placed by the rider and went unanswered. And the rider's own track places her within the STANDARD presence radius of 100 m on every one of her 194 qualifying fixes, at a maximum of 15.3 m from the pin. All three limbs hold — full refund, no driver compensation. I state the timestamps plainly so the Judge can see the one point the driver could contest: the message and the rider's in-radius fixes sit in the period before the 19:33:55 arrival marker (the rider's track runs 19:02:40 to 19:31:37), and if the Judge reads the 'waiting window' as beginning only at the arrival marker, limb (a) is untimed on these facts. Even on that narrower reading the driver never communicated at any point in the trip.

The rider's own trace shows she did the thing the fee assumes she did not. Her device reports 194 fixes between 19:02:40 and 19:31:37, all stationary (distinct speed 0.0), at distances from the pin of between 4.9 m and 15.3 m. The driver's track, over the same trip, has a mean distance of 356 m from the pin and a maximum of 745 m, and its only sustained in-radius presence is the 230-second run immediately before he cancelled. This is not a rider who failed to be at the pickup point.

The deciding evidence is clean and at full weight, so no impairment caps the ruling and no POL-NS-09(e) escalation arises. The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0: coverage_pct 100, 223 fixes at a 10-second cadence, gaps [] and max_gap_sec 0.0, so no POL-NS-08(b) trace defect. The 'arrived' event at 19:33:55 matches the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 19:33:50 to within 5 seconds, so there is no POL-NS-08(a) clock skew. The fare line also reconciles: SGD 4.00 equals the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00), so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and the charge is the right amount, which is precisely why refunding it is the complete remedy.

Nothing in the profiles supports escalating this case rather than ruling it. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and both rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) fires. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is also not met: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 110 is a rate of under 0.01, far below 0.08. There is no abuse pattern on either side to send to a reviewer.

The money is exact and the remedy is complete on these facts: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 and total_charged is 4.00, with base fare, distance fare, time fare and platform fee all 0.00. The whole contested amount is the cancellation-fee line, and a full refund of it returns exactly SGD 4.00 to the rider without touching any other line, as POL-GEN-03 requires.

If the Judge reaches POL-NS-03 at all, neither of its fault-allocation branches helps the driver. trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill of limb (ii) — the only route by which a driver in a wrong-entrance case is paid — cannot apply. And the rider had already named her position in the chat ('I'm at Blk 12 pickup point'), so under limb (i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation for stationary fixes outside the arrival radius. Either way the rider keeps the refund and the driver recovers nothing from her.

claims.text: The rider's account — that the driver was 'four hundred metres away' and 'never came' — is contradicted by the driver's own device trace: it records 24 consecutive fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, the closest of them 8.0 m from the pickup pin, so the arrival test in POL-NS-02 is met and the driver did physically reach the pickup point.

The 'arrived' marker is genuine and POL-NS-05 is not engaged: the trace already places the driver inside the 50 m arrival radius at 19:33:50, five seconds before the 19:33:55 arrived event, and the single in-geofence interval that follows is one in which he held position, so the marker was not laid more than 300 m out and was not laid from motion, and no false-arrival finding under POL-NS-05 (i) or (ii) arises.

The rider was not at the pickup point while the driver was there. The rider's own device track runs from 19:02:40 and stops at 19:31:37 — two minutes and eighteen seconds before the driver's first in-geofence fix at 19:33:50 — so the rider track carries no fix at all across the driver's waiting window, and limb (c) of POL-NS-04, which requires the rider inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius for the MAJORITY of qualifying fixes across that window, cannot be satisfied on this record; at best it is undecidable, and POL-NS-04's own rule makes an undecidable rider_presence neutral rather than exonerating, so POL-NS-04 gives the rider nothing.

There is no integrity defect in the charge itself: fare_breakdown's cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 is exactly the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee under the fee schedule's resolution rule, so the charge reconciles with the schedule and the rider gains nothing from POL-NS-08(d); the fee is displaced, if at all, only by a substantive clause, not by any defect in the amount or the ledger.

The rider's insinuation that the driver should be barred from taking work is unsupported by the only profile test the no-show policy runs on a driver: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip, because 1 no-show termination in the trailing 30 days is far below the 4-or-more limb and 1 termination over 110 completed trips is far below the 0.08 rate limb, so the profile carries no adverse finding and this is not a fee-farming case.

On the decisive arithmetic the driver does not overstate his position: the trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1) in which he held position from 19:33:50 to 19:37:40, 230 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a shortfall of 70 seconds, and no accumulation is available under POL-NS-06(i) because EV-ADVIS-00613-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and that limb requires an advisory that is present and populated. The miss is therefore confined to POL-NS-01 limb (c) alone, while limbs (a), (b) and (d) are established on clean, full-weight evidence; the driver's arrival and the rider's absence at the pin are proven facts, and the shortfall should not be inflated into a false-arrival or fee-farming finding.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is for both of you. The dispute is the SGD 4.00 cancellation (no-show) fee on trip TRP-00613, filed by the rider.

What decides it is the holding time, not the arrival. POL-NS-01 is a four-limb test and all four must hold for the fee to stand. Limbs (a), (b) are met: the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 19:33:55 and the driver's device trace puts him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius at 19:33:50, five seconds earlier, with 24 qualifying fixes and a closest approach of about 8 m. But limb (c) fails on the driver's own numbers. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'arrived' tap. The trace shows one continuous in-geofence run, 19:33:50 to 19:37:40 — 230 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a shortfall of 70 seconds. Because limb (c) fails, the fee is not chargeable, and limb (d) cannot rescue it either, since the required dwell never elapsed.

POL-NS-06 then states the consequence directly: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum, the cancellation fee is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages, and no driver compensation is payable. The one route to accumulate dwell across separate intervals, POL-NS-06(i), is unavailable twice over: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00613-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact and cannot qualify; and the trace records only one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to add. The driver's account that he was held up by an accident therefore has nothing behind it in the record.

The driver's arrival marker is nonetheless genuine, and I accept that: the 'arrived' event sits five seconds after the first in-geofence fix, inside the radius and with the driver stationary, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged and no false-arrival finding (and no POL-NS-05(ii) referral) arises. POL-NS-03 is not reached either: the driver did hold position inside the arrival radius, so this is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case, and its goodwill and compensation branches do not apply. The rider's 'four hundred metres away' description is not borne out for the arrival itself — the driver's trip-wide mean distance of 356 m and maximum of 745 m describe his approach, not his position during the hold — but that does not matter, because the shortfall alone defeats the fee.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full before it pays anything, and it is not; POL-NS-06 also states that no compensation is payable on a shortfall. The anti-farming check would not have tripped anyway: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 110 is far below the 0.08 rate, so the profile carries no adverse finding against the driver and the rider's suggestion that he be barred from work is not supported by any test this policy runs.

The money is exact. The cancellation-fee line is SGD 4.00, which equals the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so the charge reconciled with the fee schedule and no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises; refunding that line returns the whole contested SGD 4.00 and touches no other line. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

The rider's separate POL-NS-04 exoneration argument does not change the outcome, and I note the difficulty with it: her locating message at 19:08:40 and her in-radius fixes (4.9 m to 15.3 m from the pin) sit before the driver's waiting window, and her track ends at 19:31:37, so limb (c) across that window is at best undecidable. It makes no difference: the refund is full under POL-NS-06 regardless of where the rider was.

On confidence and escalation: the deciding evidence is clean and at full weight. The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 — coverage 100%, 223 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 — the 'arrived' event matches the first in-geofence fix to within 5 seconds (no clock skew), the chat count matches the trip record, and the fare reconciles. No POL-NS-08 limb is engaged. Neither profile shows a counterparty dispute pattern (both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0; no_show_disputes_30d is 0), so no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger fires and no referral is produced.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the arithmetic of the hold decides this case, and no integrity defect complicates it.

To the rider: your dispute is upheld. The cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 is refunded to you in full. To the driver: the fee is refunded because the wait was too short. This is a refund to the rider; no amount is charged to you.
